definition: Relating to or providing pleasure through the physical senses, especially in a sexually suggestive or pleasurable way; implies slow, touch-oriented eroticism rather than crude explicitness.
Relating to or tending to arouse sexual desire or excitement; erotic in content, tone, or imagery.
Fiery and sexually passionate; describes someone with intense burning sexual energy or vigor, especially as a lover.
notes: From fuego (fire); implies active combustive sexual energy rather than mere desire; more common in Latin American Spanish and romance registers.

definition: Burning, ardent; describes intensely passionate romantic or sexual desire, most often in literary or poetic contexts.
notes: More literary and less colloquial than fogoso; frequently appears in romantic literature and song lyrics rather than everyday speech.

definition: Slang for someone persistently or annoyingly sexually aroused; a randy or horny person.
notes: Primarily Iberian Spanish; informal diminutive-augmentative of caliente (hot); mildly derogatory; also spelled calentorra for feminine.

definition: Having a prurient or morbidly fascinated interest in something transgressive, forbidden, or sexual; titillating in an unhealthy way.
notes: In Spanish, el morbo is a noun for the specific frisson of transgressive titillation; morboso describes the person or stimulus producing it; the English 'prurient' captures only part of the meaning.

definition: A sexually dirty or filthy person; someone with crude, depraved, or gratuitously vulgar sexual behavior or tastes.
notes: Intensified diminutive of guarro/a (pig, dirty); predominantly Iberian Spanish; refers specifically to sexual filthiness rather than general uncleanliness.

definition: Pig; used as a sexual insult for someone lecherous, sexually depraved, or behaving in a crude and dirty manner.
notes: Primary meaning is the animal; in sexual contexts implies someone who behaves with crude carnal depravity or makes unwanted advances.

definition: Dirty or risqué in a sexual sense; used to describe sexually suggestive jokes, humor, or content, as in chiste verde (dirty joke).
notes: Color-coded euphemism parallel to English 'blue' for sexually suggestive content; universally understood across all Spanish dialects.

definition: A person given to vice or sexual excess; someone with strong, possibly deviant sexual appetites who pursues pleasure without moral restraint.
notes: From vicio (vice); implies someone who has surrendered to carnal excess; softer than pervertido — implies appetite rather than clinical deviance.

definition: A pervert; a person with deviant, socially unacceptable, or transgressive sexual interests or behavior.
Frigid; lacking sexual responsiveness or desire; applied most often pejoratively to women perceived as unresponsive to sexual advances.
notes: Has both clinical and colloquial-pejorative registers; applied disproportionately as a gendered insult toward women.

definition: Literally extinguished or switched off; colloquially used of someone with very low sexual energy, passion, or libido.
notes: General Spanish word for dimmed or turned off; in sexual contexts contrasts directly with fogoso/a or ardiente as its antonym.

definition: Impotent; unable to achieve or sustain an erection; also used figuratively for someone helpless or without power.
notes: Functions both as a clinical descriptor and as a general pejorative for weakness or ineffectiveness; figurative use dilutes sexual specificity.

definition: Anorgasmic; clinically unable to achieve orgasm despite normal or adequate sexual stimulation.
notes: Strictly clinical; no dedicated anorgasmic slug in the registry; mapped to sexual_frigidity as nearest available — the conditions are clinically distinct (absent orgasm vs. absent desire).

definition: Without libido; having no sexual drive or desire; a clinical phrase used colloquially to describe absent or very low sexual appetite.
notes: Two-word phrase; loanword libido entered Spanish via psychoanalytic terminology; sits in clinical register even in casual speech.

definition: A person sexually and romantically attracted to people of the same sex; the clinical Spanish term corresponding to English homosexual.
notes: Increasingly displaced by gay in everyday speech; homosexual now reads as clinical, formal, or conservative in most Spanish-speaking contexts.

definition: A person sexually attracted primarily to people of a different sex; the clinical term for straight orientation.
A person sexually or romantically attracted to both men and women, or to more than one gender.
A person who experiences little or no sexual attraction to others; used both as a clinical descriptor and as a self-identity label.
notes: Recognition has grown substantially among younger Spanish speakers in the 2010s–2020s alongside broader LGBTQ+ visibility.

definition: A person sexually and romantically attracted to others regardless of their sex or gender identity.
notes: Loanword from English; recognition rising among younger and urban Spanish speakers but still limited among older demographics.

definition: A woman sexually and romantically attracted to other women; the standard Spanish term for lesbian, used both clinically and colloquially.
notes: Can be deployed as a slur in hostile contexts but functions primarily as the standard neutral term; widely reclaimed within the community.

definition: Gay; a person, especially a man, sexually attracted to people of the same sex; the dominant everyday term across all Spanish-speaking regions.
notes: Loanword from English; has largely displaced homosexual in conversational use across Spain and Latin America.

definition: A person whose gender identity differs from the sex assigned at birth, especially one who has pursued or undergone hormonal or surgical transition; the older Spanish clinical term.
notes: Note single 's' in Spanish spelling; increasingly considered dated or overly clinical by activists and medical bodies, being replaced by transgénero in formal contexts.

definition: Transgender; a person whose gender identity differs from the sex assigned at birth; the contemporary preferred term in Spanish medical, legal, and activist discourse.
notes: Loanword/calque from English; increasingly preferred over transexual in formal and activist contexts; recognition still lower than transexual among older generations.
